{{family name hatnote|Fernández|Betriu|lang=Catalan}}
'''Ricard Fernández Betriu''' (born 19 March 1999), also known as '''Cucu''', is an Andorran footballer who plays for [[CE Casa de Portugal]].<ref>[https://us.soccerway.com/players/ricard-fernandez/379961/ Soccerway Profile]</ref>

==International career==
Fernández made his senior debut for the [[Andorra national football team]] in a 1–0 friendly win over [[Liechtenstein national football team|Liechtenstein]] on 21 March 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://us.soccerway.com/matches/2018/03/21/world/friendlies/liechtenstein/andorra/2742689/|title=Liechtenstein vs. Andorra – 21 March 2018 – Soccerway|website=us.soccerway.com}}</ref> He has remained in the under-21 set up since, however, notably scoring a brace in a shock 3–3 draw with [[England national under-21 football team|England]] in October 2020, securing Andorra under-21s a rare point against a team featuring [[Premier League]] players such as [[Eddie Nketiah]] and [[Aaron Ramsdale]].<ref>[https://www.skysports.com/football/andorra-u21-vs-england-u21/406216 Andorra U21s 3-3 England U21s: Eddie Nketiah denied late winner as hosts equalize in stoppage time] Sky Sports. 7 October 2020. Retrieved 20 October 2020.</ref> On 12 November 2021, he received a red card for elbowing [[Kamil Glik]] in the first minute of the match vs [[Poland national football team|Poland]], which Andorra went on to lose by a score of 1–4.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/international/scottish-ref-john-beaton-red-cards-player-after-20-seconds-in-andorra-v-poland-world-cup-qualifier-3456779|author=Sked, Joel|publisher=scotsman.com|title=Scottish ref John Beaton red cards player after 20 seconds in Andorra v Poland World Cup qualifier|date=12 November 2021|access-date=15 November 2021|language=en}}</ref>

Fernández scored his first goal for Andorra on 12 October 2021 during a 3–0 win against [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]] during [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group I|2022 FIFA World Cup qualification]], and the match subsequently became Andorra's first ever away victory.

Fernández scored his second goal for Andorra on 21 March 2024 during a 1–1 draw against [[South Africa national soccer team|South Africa]] during the [[2024 FIFA Series|2024 FIFA Series: Algeria]].
